tier_reason: Independent third-party harness (axiolid/benchmarks, Rust + cpp/shim.cpp, public) times Manifold v3.5.1 against CGAL PMP corefinement with correctness oracles; sphere A-B at 1.31M tris/operand: manifold 2816.2 ms vs cgal 13368.2 ms. CPU model and compiler are not stated ('20-core host', default Release flags), so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Third-party axiolid benchmark, two icospheres of 1,310,720 triangles each: A-B Manifold 2,816.2 ms vs CGAL 13,368.2 ms (4.7x); union 3,462.5 vs 23,922.9 ms (6.9x); intersection 2,248.7 vs 5,602.2 ms (2.5x) (ratios derived from page data). Smaller subdivisions show 2.6-5.6x. On a Menger sponge only Manifold completed past depth 1 (CGAL corefinement failed). Author's blog: single-thread 'an order of magnitude faster' than OpenSCAD fast-csg, GPU '100-1,000 times faster than the current OpenSCAD release'.
corrections.workload: Mesh booleans (union, intersection, A-B) of two overlapping icospheres from 5,120 to 1,310,720 triangles per operand, plus Menger-sponge and wall-with-openings cases (axiolid cross-kernel benchmark); author's blog: sphere differences and Menger sponge vs OpenSCAD+CGAL.
corrections.caveats: Evidence is from a 0-star repo of a competing kernel (axiolid, no LICENSE file), with CPU model and compiler unstated and best of 1 rep; Manifold's own README gives no numbers. Manifold was built with TBB parallelism on a 20-core host versus serial CGAL. Blog baseline is OpenSCAD (CGAL-based), not CGAL directly. Axiolid's own analytic box path beats Manifold on axis-aligned Menger cases, which is not a general boolean.

notes: Numbers verified in axiolid/benchmarks README (Sphere-sphere section). Metadata matches: Apache-2.0, 2.2k stars, last commit 2026-09-30. Blog numbers not re-opened.

tier_reason: First-party README states benchmark compilation 35.3 s (Boost) vs 1.4 s (THST) and has runtime charts vs Boost.Geometry rtree from code in benchmark/ (CPU i7-4870HQ stated), but the compiler and flags are not stated (Xcode Release build implied), so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 'benchmark compilation: 35,3 sec vs 1,4 sec' versus Boost (about 25x, derived from page data). Runtime charts only: per benchmark/README, Boost.Geometry bulk-loading/rstar gives the best query times, THST quadratic custom comes next; in the dynamic case THST quadratic beats bgi linear above ~400 objects.
corrections.caveats: Speed claim is compile time; at runtime Boost.Geometry rtree (bulk/rstar) is faster for query per the project's own benchmark README, and THST wins only the dynamic case above ~400 objects vs bgi linear. Runtime values only in PNG charts. Compiler/flags not stated; setup copied from mloskot/spatial_index_benchmark. Old hardware and OS (macOS Sierra).

notes: Not faster at runtime overall; keep as a compile-time win and record the runtime shortcoming. Metadata matches: MIT, 133 stars, last commit 2024-03-16 (stale).
